buyers.why_relevant: 1c finder fee: Active sector roll-up with a clear, repeatable appetite (legal/professional services succession) and an explicit buy-and-build pipeline, meaning recurring acquisition need. Ola can introduce retiring law/professional-services firm owners for finder fees on bolt-on deals.

buyers.name: WebStreet
buyers.specialties: Micro-PE fund acquiring profitable online businesses - SaaS, e-commerce, content/media, and service-based - typically in the c.$100k-$2M range. 50+ assets acquired, $50M+ raised; partners with operators to buy and grow.
buyers.region: UK & Ireland eligible (global online businesses; remote/digital)
buyers.contact: Deal submission / 'sell your business' route at webstreet.co; deals@webstreet.co
buyers.why_relevant: 1c finder fee: Active, well-capitalised micro-PE acquirer with a public deal-submission route and a steady acquisition cadence. Ideal for Ola to introduce profitable UK/Irish online/SaaS/e-commerce founders; digital businesses are location-agnostic so the UK/IE seller base maps cleanly to WebStreet's mandate.

buyers.name: SureSwift Capital
buyers.specialties: Long-established serial acquirer of profitable bootstrapped B2B SaaS businesses from independent founders. Buys, holds and grows; helped pioneer the SaaS roll-up model. Typically small-to-mid recurring-revenue SaaS.
buyers.region: UK & Ireland eligible (acquires globally / remote SaaS)
buyers.contact: 'Sell Your Business' submission form at sureswiftcapital.com
buyers.why_relevant: 1c finder fee: One of the most credible and durable SaaS acquirers with a dedicated public seller-submission funnel. Ola can introduce UK/Irish bootstrapped SaaS founders looking for a clean exit; SureSwift's track record makes it an easy, trusted name to bring sellers to for introduction fees.

buyers.name: Acquire.com (formerly MicroAcquire)
buyers.specialties: Online acquisition marketplace for profitable internet businesses - SaaS, e-commerce, content, services. 500k+ qualified buyers and thousands of vetted listings; connects sellers directly to micro-PE, search funds and individual acquirers.
buyers.contact: Seller listing/onboarding at acquire.com (free seller listings; buyer network access)
buyers.why_relevant: 1c finder fee: A distribution platform rather than a single buyer - lets Ola place UK/Irish online-business sellers in front of a large pool of vetted acquirers at once. Useful both as a place to list referred sellers and as a hunting ground to identify named individual acquirers for direct finder-fee intros.

buyers.name: Business Sale Report (business-sale.com)
buyers.specialties: 30+ year UK businesses-for-sale marketplace and deal-flow platform across all SME sectors (professional/financial, retail, online, distressed). £8bn+ cumulative deal flow; carries listings from owner-sellers, brokers and intermediaries plus a buyer/acquirer membership base.
buyers.contact: List-a-business / sell-a-business route at business-sale.com; member enquiry desk
buyers.why_relevant: 1c finder fee: Established marketplace and acquirer network giving Ola a route to both list referred sellers and connect them to its membership of active UK/Irish buyers and roll-up funds. Strong, credible UK-and-Ireland coverage makes it a practical channel for sourcing and placing seller introductions.

ireland.sourcing_criteria: Target profitable, established SMEs with a weak or outdated digital presence that also fit the funding eligibility windows — that overlap is where you broker deals. (1) PROFITABILITY/STABILITY filter: trading 6+ months (ideally 2+ years), positive cash flow or visible demand (busy premises, queues, good Google reviews 4.0+ with volume, active social proof). Use CRO.ie company search and abridged accounts to confirm the entity is registered and not dormant; rules of thumb: turnover under EUR2m and under 10 employees fits the LEO/TOV micro-band, 10-50 employees and exporting fits Enterprise Ireland/Grow Digital. (2) WEAK-DIGITAL signals: no website or one that is non-responsive/HTTP-only/slow (test on PageSpeed Insights, score under 50), no e-commerce/online booking, no Google Business Profile or unclaimed listing, last social post 6+ months old, no SSL, .ie domain not owned. Scrape these via Google Maps categories + filtering, Hostinger/registrar WHOIS for .ie ownership, and BuiltWith to detect missing analytics/checkout. (3) FUNDING-MATCH filter: cross-reference each prospect against eligibility — micro-business (under 10 staff, under EUR2m turnover, trading 6+ months, no prior TOV) = Trading Online Voucher/Grow Digital candidate; 1-50 staff that completed Digital for Business = Grow Digital; 10+ staff already exporting = Enterprise Ireland Digital Marketing Capability / Digital Transition Fund. (4) SECTOR targeting: retail, hospitality, trades, professional services, food producers and tourism operators are the highest-density pool of grant-eligible, weak-digital, profitable firms. (5) SOURCING THE FUNDING YOURSELF: register as / partner with an approved supplier, attend the LEO 'Digital for Business' / pre-qualifying training so you can guide clients through approval, and build relationships with the 31 Local Enterprise Offices and Enterprise Ireland Development Advisers to get referred to grant-approved clients. DEAL MECHANIC: lead with 'we get the State to pay ~50% of your new website/e-commerce build' — you scope a project at e.g. EUR5,000, the client claims EUR2,500 TOV (or up to EUR5,000 Grow Digital), so their net cost halves and your close rate rises. Always confirm approval is granted BEFORE any spend, since costs incurred pre-approval are not reimbursable.

schemes.body: Local Enterprise Office (LEO) network of 31 offices, under the Dept. of Enterprise, Trade & Employment / Enterprise Ireland. Note: TOV is being superseded/folded into the Grow Digital Voucher from 2024-2026; many LEOs now route website/e-commerce funding through Grow Digital, but TOV references and the up-to-EUR2,500 ~50% website grant remain the canonical entry-level scheme.
schemes.funds: Website development, e-commerce and online payment/booking systems, digital marketing and online advertising (up to 50% of voucher), app development, subscriptions to low-cost online retail platforms, and digital training.
schemes.match_or_cap: 50% of eligible costs up to a maximum EUR2,500 (ex VAT) — i.e. EUR2,500 covers a EUR5,000 spend. Whichever is the lesser of EUR2,500 or 50%.
schemes.eligibility: Microenterprise: fewer than 10 employees, turnover under EUR2 million, trading at least 6 months, located in Republic of Ireland, and not having previously received a Trading Online Voucher. Must attend a pre-qualifying/Digital training session and get the application APPROVED before incurring any expenditure.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: Lead-gen hook: pitch a EUR5,000 website/e-commerce build to a sub-10-employee local business and have them apply for the EUR2,500 TOV so the State part-funds the build we deliver. We help them through the LEO training and approval, scope the quote to maximise eligible spend, then build the site once approved. Halves their net cost, raises our close rate, positions us as the grant-savvy supplier.

schemes.body: Local Enterprise Office (LEO) network / National Enterprise Hub (neh.gov.ie), Dept. of Enterprise, Trade & Employment. This is the enhanced successor to the Trading Online Voucher, raising entry-level digital support to EUR5,000.
schemes.funds: Software adoption and subscriptions (CRM, inventory/stock management, analytics, cybersecurity, cloud accounting, job-tracking, workflow, e-invoicing), e-commerce platforms, plus associated training and IT configuration/setup support.
schemes.match_or_cap: 50% of eligible costs, up to a maximum EUR5,000 (minimum grant EUR500). Businesses can apply for up to two projects but the combined cap stays at EUR5,000.
schemes.eligibility: 1 to 50 paid employees, established and actively trading for a minimum of 6 months, registered/operating in the LEO's area, and must have completed a free 'Digital for Business' consultancy project (up to 3 days with an approved digital consultant) within the last 2 years as a prerequisite.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: Bigger-ticket version of the TOV play for 1-50 employee firms. We steer the client into the free Digital for Business assessment (which itself surfaces the digital roadmap we then deliver), then build/configure their e-commerce, CRM or workflow tooling with up to EUR5,000 (and up to two projects) part-funded. We can sell the build PLUS the recurring software/config work that the voucher reimburses.

schemes.body: Local Enterprise Office (LEO) network, Dept. of Enterprise, Trade & Employment.
schemes.funds: Fully-funded (free) digital advisory: an approved digital consultant spends up to ~3 days with the business to produce a digital action plan / roadmap covering website, e-commerce, CRM, marketing and operations.
schemes.match_or_cap: 100% funded (free to the business) — no cash match required; it is the mandatory gateway to the Grow Digital Voucher.
schemes.eligibility: Small businesses, typically up to 50 employees, registered in the LEO area and trading. Acts as the prerequisite assessment for accessing the Grow Digital Voucher.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: We position as / partner with the approved consultant, or shadow the output: the roadmap this programme produces becomes the spec for the paid website/e-commerce/CRM project we then deliver and that the Grow Digital Voucher part-funds. It is a free, State-run sales funnel into our build work.

schemes.scheme: Enterprise Ireland Digital Marketing Capability Grant
schemes.body: Enterprise Ireland (national development agency, Dept. of Enterprise, Trade & Employment).
schemes.funds: External training/advisory from a qualified digital marketing consultant, development of a digital marketing strategy, and a portion of the salary of an internal project champion implementing the strategy. Aimed at strengthening online presence and international market reach.
schemes.match_or_cap: Up to 50% of eligible project costs, to a maximum grant of EUR35,000.
schemes.eligibility: Established SMEs / larger companies that are Enterprise Ireland clients (or eligible to become clients), typically more than 10 full-time employees and already exporting (or with clear export ambition) outside Ireland.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: For our larger, exporting clients we scope a digital marketing strategy + implementation engagement and have them claim up to EUR35,000 (50%) under this grant. We act as the qualified consultant/agency delivering the strategy, SEO, paid media and analytics build — the grant funds half of a high-value retainer rather than a one-off website.

schemes.scheme: Enterprise Ireland Digital Transition Fund (incl. Digital Process Innovation)
schemes.body: Enterprise Ireland, funded under Ireland's National Recovery & Resilience Plan (EUR85m 'Grow Digital' fund to 2026), Dept. of Enterprise, Trade & Employment.
schemes.funds: Digital transformation projects across the spectrum: going online, e-commerce/export enablement, adoption of digital technologies to reach new markets, and deeper Digital Process Innovation (automation, data, integrated systems) to improve productivity.
schemes.match_or_cap: 50% of eligible costs. Smaller project types range EUR5,000-EUR35,000; the Digital Process Innovation strand goes up to a maximum grant of EUR150,000 (50%).
schemes.eligibility: Enterprise Ireland client companies employing 10+ full-time staff at application; High Potential Start-Up clients employing 5+ full-time staff are also eligible.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: Our top-tier offer for scaling EI-client manufacturers/exporters. We package a larger digital transformation programme (e-commerce platform, system integration, automation, data tooling) and use the fund to cover 50% — up to EUR35,000 for online/market projects or up to EUR150,000 for process-innovation builds — letting us land multi-phase, high-value implementation contracts that the State half-funds.

schemes.body: Local Enterprise Office (LEO) network, Dept. of Enterprise, Trade & Employment.
schemes.funds: Start-up costs in a new business's first 18 months: capital/equipment, salary support, marketing and (within that) website/digital setup, and other eligible establishment costs.
schemes.match_or_cap: Up to 50% of eligible investment, maximum EUR150,000 (grants over EUR80,000 up to EUR150,000 are exceptional and reserved for projects with potential to graduate to Enterprise Ireland). Note the grant is typically 30% refundable to the LEO over 36 months.
schemes.eligibility: New micro/small businesses (generally under 10 employees) within the first 18 months of setting up, registered in the LEO area, with growth/job-creation and ideally export potential. Sole traders, partnerships and companies in manufacturing or internationally-traded services are favoured.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: For brand-new clients we fold the website/branding/digital-marketing line into their Priming Grant application as part of overall start-up investment, so up to 50% of our setup work is grant-aided. We help them frame the digital spend within the broader business plan the LEO funds.

schemes.body: Local Enterprise Office (LEO) network, Dept. of Enterprise, Trade & Employment.
schemes.funds: Growth/expansion costs for established micro-businesses beyond 18 months: capital, salary support, consultancy, and marketing/digital expansion (website upgrades, e-commerce scaling, digital marketing).
schemes.match_or_cap: Up to 50% of eligible costs, commonly up to ~EUR150,000 maximum (amount varies by LEO budget); like the Priming Grant a portion is typically refundable.
schemes.eligibility: Established micro-enterprises (under 10 employees, turnover under EUR2m) trading more than 18 months, registered in the LEO area, demonstrating growth and job-creation/export potential.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: Where a profitable established micro-business has outgrown its current site, we position a website re-platform / e-commerce upgrade / digital marketing scale-up inside their Business Expansion Grant so the State covers ~50% of a larger redevelopment than the EUR2,500 TOV alone would fund.

schemes.body: Local Enterprise Office (LEO) network, Dept. of Enterprise, Trade & Employment.
schemes.funds: Investigating the viability of a new product/service/market: market research, consultancy, technical development, prototyping/innovation, research labour, and related miscellaneous costs.
schemes.match_or_cap: 50% of eligible costs (60% in the Border, Midlands & West region) up to a maximum of EUR15,000.
schemes.eligibility: Micro/small businesses and start-ups (generally under 10 employees, turnover under EUR2m) registered in the LEO area, exploring a new product/service or market with innovation/export potential.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: We use this to fund the discovery phase of larger digital projects — e.g. market research, UX research, technical prototype of an e-commerce or app concept — billing the research/prototyping as the feasibility study (50-60% grant-aided), which then de-risks and seeds the full build we quote afterwards under TOV/Grow Digital.

ukScotland.sourcing_criteria: To self-source and broker these deals, target businesses where (1) a fundable government scheme exists for their profile and (2) their current digital presence is weak enough that an agency build/upgrade creates obvious uplift. Concrete sourcing filters: (a) Sector + region match to a scheme — e.g. SME manufacturers (5-249 staff) in England's North East/North West/West Midlands/West of England/Yorkshire & Humber/London for Made Smarter; any Scottish SME trading 6+ months for DigitalBoost; Highlands & Islands businesses for HIE's Digital & Technology Adoption grant; businesses with 5-249 employees trading 12+ months for Help to Grow: Management. (b) Turnover/size signals — Companies House filings showing turnover under GBP45m (GGS), profitable (positive retained earnings / net assets growing), 1+ years trading. Profitable + weak-digital is the sweet spot: they have cashflow to cover the match portion and a viable proposition lenders/grant bodies will back. (c) Weak-digital signals to score leads: no website or one that fails Lighthouse/Core Web Vitals, no HTTPS, no e-commerce despite a product business, no Google Business Profile, thin/no social, no booking/payment integration, dated copyright year, not mobile-responsive. Scrape these via Google Maps + Companies House + BuiltWith/Wappalyzer. (d) Geography overlay — cross-reference the business's local authority against live UKSPF grant rounds (each council runs its own GBP2.5k-GBP10k+ business growth/productivity grants with ~40-60% match), and Scottish region against Business Gateway / SOSE / HIE catchments. Brokering workflow: identify a weak-digital but profitable target -> match it to the scheme that covers the largest share (e.g. DigitalBoost up to GBP25k at ~50%, Made Smarter up to GBP20k at 50%, UKSPF growth grant) -> approach the business with a 'we handle the grant paperwork + build the site/e-commerce/automation for a net cost after grant' pitch -> the agency becomes the named supplier on the application (most schemes require quotes from a supplier, so position the agency's quote as one of the required quotes) -> on approval, the grant pays the match-eligible portion direct or as reimbursement and the client pays the remaining match share. For loan-funded deals (GGS, no grant cap) target larger projects where the client borrows up to GBP2m at preferential terms to fund a multi-month digital growth retainer. Highest-conversion combos: Scottish VAT-registered SME + DigitalBoost (up to GBP25k); England SME manufacturer + Made Smarter (GBP20k); any UK SME senior leader + Help to Grow: Management (90% subsidised, builds the relationship then upsell the build); local-authority-matched UKSPF growth grant for micro businesses.

schemes.body: British Business Bank (UK government-owned), delivered via accredited lenders (NatWest, etc.). Available UK-wide including Scotland via Find Business Support.
schemes.funds: Government-backed guarantee on commercial debt finance: term loans, overdrafts, asset finance, invoice finance and asset-based lending. Funds can be used for growth investment including digital transformation, software, e-commerce platforms, equipment and working capital.
schemes.match_or_cap: 70% government-backed guarantee to the lender; facility sizes up to GBP2m (up to GBP1m for borrowers in scope of the Northern Ireland Protocol). No grant cap - it is a loan; the business remains 100% liable for repayment.
schemes.eligibility: UK-based smaller businesses with group turnover up to GBP45m, carrying out trading activity in the UK with generally more than 50% of income from trading. Lender must judge the business proposition viable; business must not be 'in difficulty' or in insolvency proceedings. Scheme extended to at least 31 March 2030 (per 2025 Spending Review).
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: Position large multi-month digital growth projects (full e-commerce rebuilds, marketing retainers, automation, ERP/CRM integration) as growth investment the client funds via a GGS-backed loan. The agency does not touch the loan - it pitches the project, and the client borrows up to GBP2m at preferential, government-de-risked terms. Best for ambitious projects above grant caps where there is no free-money ceiling.

schemes.body: Made Smarter (UK government / DBT-backed), delivered regionally in England (North East, North West, West Midlands, West of England, Yorkshire & Humber, London).
schemes.funds: Capital Expenditure (CapEx) matched grants plus specialist advice/consultancy to adopt digital manufacturing technology: automation, robotics, AI, 3D printing, IoT/sensors and data-driven tools. Also funds digital leadership training and fully funded digital internships.
schemes.match_or_cap: Up to 50% match funding, capped at GBP20,000 per project (business must contribute at least 50%).
schemes.eligibility: Small and medium-sized manufacturing and engineering businesses with manufacturing premises in England, in one of the participating regions. Currently England-only (no Scotland equivalent under Made Smarter; Scottish manufacturers use HIE / Scottish Enterprise / DigitalBoost instead).
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: For SME manufacturer clients, the agency acts as the digital technology supplier/specialist advisor. It scopes a data, IoT, automation or software project, supplies the required quote, and the Made Smarter grant covers up to 50% (max GBP20k) of the build/tooling - the agency invoices the full project, client pays the matched portion plus the grant reimbursement.

schemes.scheme: UK Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF) Business Growth / Productivity Grants
schemes.body: UK Government (MHCLG), administered locally by individual local authorities / combined authorities (each runs its own grant scheme and criteria). UK-wide including Scottish councils.
schemes.funds: Local business growth and productivity capital grants. Commonly fund websites, e-commerce, digital marketing, software/CRM, equipment and productivity-improving capital - exact eligible spend set by each council.
schemes.match_or_cap: Typically GBP2,500 to GBP10,000+ per business, with match funding usually required (commonly ~40-60% applicant contribution, e.g. minimum 40% match). Caps and match vary by local authority.
schemes.eligibility: Micro and small SMEs (often <=50 FTE) located in the administering council's area, usually trading at least 12 months, able to provide match funding and quotes. Must align to the local Sustainable Economic Growth Strategy (local jobs, productivity, sustainability). Note: 2025/26 was a transition year - spend deadlines (e.g. 31 Jan 2026) apply, so check live rounds.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: Cross-reference each prospect's local authority for a live UKSPF round, then pitch a website/e-commerce/digital-marketing package sized to the council's grant cap. The agency supplies the required quote and becomes the named supplier; the grant covers its share (~40-60%) and the client pays the rest - effectively a discounted build funded by the council.

schemes.body: UK Government (Department for Business & Trade) via the Small Business Charter and ~accredited UK business schools (Birkbeck, Aston, Leeds, UWE, etc.). UK-wide including Scotland.
schemes.funds: 12-week senior-leader management/scale-up programme: 50 hours of training across digital marketing, strategy, leadership, innovation and financial management, plus 1:1 business mentoring and a peer network. (Training subsidy, not a cash grant.)
schemes.match_or_cap: 90% government-subsidised. Full cost ~GBP7,500; participant pays just GBP750.
schemes.eligibility: Senior leaders of SMEs from any sector, operating more than 1 year, with between 5 and 249 employees. Registered via the Small Business Charter; cohorts running through 2026 (e.g. June 2026, Sept 2026 starts).
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: Use as a low-cost relationship and lead-gen wedge: encourage SME-owner prospects onto the 90%-subsidised course (it explicitly covers digital marketing), positioning the agency as the implementation partner who executes the digital growth plan the client builds during the course. Converts trained, growth-minded owners into retainer clients.

schemes.body: Scottish Enterprise (Scotland's national economic development agency). Covers the bulk of Scotland outside the Highlands & Islands and South of Scotland regions.
schemes.funds: R&D grants (research/develop or significantly improve a product, process or service), innovation funding, and periodic thematic digital funding calls (e.g. up to GBP50,000 per project for digital solutions in energy transition and manufacturing). A new SMART: SCOTLAND-style innovation fund is due to launch summer 2026 for high-growth companies.
schemes.match_or_cap: Varies by call. Thematic digital calls have run at up to GBP50,000 per project; R&D and innovation grants are negotiated per project with match funding typically required. (SMART: SCOTLAND historically funded a percentage of eligible project costs.)
schemes.eligibility: Scotland-based companies, generally with growth/innovation potential; specific criteria set per funding call. Many calls are time-limited and open/close periodically - check the live funding-calls list.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: For Scottish clients building genuinely new digital products/processes (custom software, platforms, AI/data tools), the agency scopes the build as an R&D or innovation project and supplies development quotes. The grant offsets a share of the build cost; the agency delivers the technical work the funding pays for.

schemes.body: Business Gateway (Scottish Government / local-authority delivered national service for Scotland).
schemes.funds: Capital grant to improve digital capability: websites, e-commerce, online booking/payment systems, digital marketing, CRM/software, cyber security and hardware/equipment that enables digital growth. Paired with free DigitalBoost advice and webinars.
schemes.match_or_cap: Matched (1:1 investment basis): up to GBP25,000 for VAT-registered businesses and up to GBP5,000 for non-VAT-registered businesses; grant awards commonly range from GBP2,000 up to GBP25,000.
schemes.eligibility: Organisations based and operating in Scotland, trading a minimum of 6 months; applicant over 18, a UK resident with the right to work. Charities, social enterprises and third-sector orgs eligible. Excluded: sex industry, politics, religion, nude/semi-nude modelling, MLM/pyramid selling, or anything that could bring the Scottish Government into disrepute.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: The flagship deal-broker for Scottish clients. Identify a VAT-registered Scottish SME with a weak/no website, scope a website + e-commerce + digital-marketing package, supply the agency's quote as the required quote, and DigitalBoost matches up to GBP25k (50% / 1:1). The agency delivers the full build; the client's net cost is roughly half.

schemes.scheme: Highlands & Islands Enterprise (HIE) Digital and Technology Adoption Capital Grant
schemes.body: Highlands and Islands Enterprise (regional economic development agency for the Highlands & Islands of Scotland).
schemes.funds: Capital grant plus specialist advice to support digital transformation and adoption of advanced digital technologies: robotics, sensors/IoT, data innovation, AI, cyber security and software development - to improve operations and efficiency.
schemes.match_or_cap: Capital grant sized to the project's requirements (negotiated); community and voluntary organisations can apply for up to GBP5,000 towards digital/technology specialist advice plus a capital grant. Programme running June 2025 to March 2029.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses and social enterprises based in the Highlands & Islands region. HIE recommends applicants have a digital action plan or feasibility study in place before enquiring.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: For clients in the Highlands & Islands, the agency first delivers (or helps fund via the GBP5k advice grant) a digital action plan/feasibility study - which HIE requires - then scopes the software/data/automation build as the capital project. The agency is the named technology supplier delivering the funded adoption work.

schemes.scheme: South of Scotland Enterprise (SOSE) Grants & Pathways Funding
schemes.body: South of Scotland Enterprise (regional economic development agency for Dumfries & Galloway and the Scottish Borders).
schemes.funds: Range of grants and tailored business support for the South of Scotland, including the Pathways Pre-Start Fund (support, mentoring and advice to set up or grow a company, delivered via Inspirent) and bespoke grants for businesses adapting, diversifying or growing - which can include digital capability.
schemes.match_or_cap: Project-specific / negotiated grants (no single published cap); Pathways Pre-Start is a GBP1m round within a GBP6m programme focused on women and under-represented groups. Match funding typically expected on capital/growth grants.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses and organisations based in the South of Scotland (Dumfries & Galloway, Scottish Borders); start-ups and growing companies, with priority strands for under-represented groups. Discuss specific projects with a SOSE adviser.
schemes.how_agency_uses_it: For South of Scotland clients, engage a SOSE adviser to fund a digital growth/diversification project, supplying the agency quote as the delivery partner. Pathways funding seeds early-stage/under-represented founders the agency can then build websites/e-commerce for, with SOSE covering a share of the cost.
